notes: Skipped discover_papers entirely for a paper it already knew by name/ID - reached the same correct answer faster and cheaper.

Correctness is identical between with_skill and without_skill across all 3 evals and 14 total assertions (pass_rate 1.0 in both configurations) - none of the current assertions discriminate skill value.

The live alphaxiv MCP tool schemas (discover_papers keywords/question/difficulty, answer_pdf_queries paper/queries) are apparently self-descriptive enough that a fresh agent constructs correct calls with zero skill guidance - the skill's main proven value this session was fixing a stale url/query signature that's no longer present in the current SKILL.md, so eval 1 is now a regression check rather than a differentiator.

The one place the skill measurably changed behavior (eval 2) made it WORSE: following the 'Code Analysis' Common Use Case's step 1 ('Use discover_papers to find the paper of interest') sent the with_skill run down a dead-end call before it fell back to naming the paper directly, costing +34% time and +24% tokens for an identical final answer. This wording is copied verbatim from the official alphaxiv docs page's own 'Common use cases' section, so the docs themselves give this advice - but it doesn't hold for the very common case where the user already names a well-known paper.
Recommended fix for iteration 2: qualify the 'Code Analysis' step 1 - skip discover_papers when the user already names a specific paper (title or arXiv ID); reserve it for open-ended discovery.

Sample size is 1 run per configuration per eval (not the usual 3) - stddev/min/max within a configuration are computed across the 3 different evals, not across repeated runs of the same eval, so they reflect eval-to-eval variance, not run-to-run noise.
